column1: Who has right of way at a roundabout?
column2: Traffic already on the roundabout.

column1: Who has priority at an unmarked crossroads where roads are of equal importance?
column2: Give way to traffic from the right and to traffic already on the junction.

column1: What must you do at a stop sign?
column2: Come to a complete stop and yield before moving off.

column1: What does a yield sign mean?
column2: Give way to traffic with priority and stop if necessary.

column1: What does a flashing amber traffic light mean?
column2: Proceed with caution only if the crossing or junction is clear; pedestrians have priority.

column1: What should you do at a steady amber traffic light?
column2: Stop unless it is unsafe to do so.

column1: What do flashing red lights at a railway crossing mean?
column2: Stop; a train is approaching or the crossing is operating.

column1: What is a filter light?
column2: A green or amber arrow that lets you proceed in that direction if it is safe and the way is clear.

column1: What are the rules for a yellow box junction?
column2: Do not enter unless you can clear it without stopping, except when turning right and waiting for a safe gap without blocking traffic with priority.

column1: What does a broken white line in the centre of the road mean?
column2: You may cross it only if it is safe to do so.

column1: What does a continuous white line in the centre of the road mean?
column2: Keep left and do not cross it except for access or in an emergency.

column1: What do double broken white lines along the centre of the road mean?
column2: They warn that continuous white lines are ahead; do not cross them unless it is safe.

column1: If there is a continuous and a broken white line together, which line do you obey?
column2: The line nearest to you.

column1: What does a broken yellow line along the side of the road mean?
column2: It marks a hard shoulder, normally for pedestrians and cyclists; you may pull in briefly to let faster traffic pass if it is safe.

column1: What does a single continuous yellow line along the side of the road mean?
column2: No parking during the times shown.
column3: official_core stephen_reviewed parking markings web_image web_remote

column1: What do double continuous yellow lines at the side of the road mean?
column2: No parking at any time.
column3: official_core stephen_reviewed parking markings web_image web_remote

column1: What do white zig-zag lines at a zebra crossing mean?
column2: No parking and no overtaking.
column3: official_core stephen_reviewed crossings markings web_image web_remote

column1: What are the road markings for no entry?
column2: A continuous and a broken white line with the words NO ENTRY.

column1: What shape are warning signs in Ireland?
column2: Diamond-shaped with a yellow background.

column1: What shape are most regulatory signs in Ireland?
column2: Circular.

column1: What colour are motorway signs?
column2: Blue.

column1: What colour are national road signs?
column2: Green.

column1: What colour are regional and local road signs?
column2: White with black text.

column1: When should you use dipped headlights?
column2: When meeting traffic, following closely, on continuously lit roads, and in fog, snow, dusk, dawn, or poor visibility.

column1: What should you do if you are dazzled by headlights?
column2: Slow down and stop if necessary; watch for pedestrians or cyclists and look towards the left verge if the dazzle is from oncoming traffic.

column1: When may you use your horn?
column2: Only to warn other road users of danger; do not use it in a built-up area between 11:30 pm and 7:00 am unless there is an emergency.

column1: What is the legal minimum tyre tread depth for a car?
column2: 1.6 mm across the central three-quarters of the tread.
column3: official_core corrected technical_checks vehicle web_image web_remote

column1: What is the 2-second rule?
column2: Leave at least 2 seconds in dry conditions, at least 4 seconds in wet conditions, and more in ice or poor conditions.

column1: How does wet weather affect braking distance?
column2: It can at least double braking distance.

column1: What is aquaplaning?
column2: When a layer of water causes the tyres to lose contact with the road, reducing steering and braking control.

column1: What is tailgating?
column2: Driving too close to the vehicle in front.

column1: What is coasting and why is it dangerous?
column2: Coasting is driving with the clutch down or in neutral; it reduces your control of the vehicle.

column1: When another driver is overtaking you, what must you not do?
column2: Increase your speed.

column1: When may you overtake on the left?
column2: When the driver ahead has moved right and signalled right, when you have signalled left, or in slow-moving traffic where the left lane is moving faster.

column1: Give examples of places where you should not overtake.
column2: Near a bend, hill crest, hump-back bridge, continuous white line, entrance, taxi rank, or where the road is too narrow or visibility is poor.

column1: How far from a junction should you not park?
column2: Within 5 metres of the junction.

column1: How far from a pedestrian crossing should you not park?
column2: Within 15 metres before it or 5 metres after it.
column3: official_core stephen_reviewed parking crossings web_image web_remote

column1: How close to the kerb should you normally park?
column2: Within 45 cm.

column1: When may you use the hard shoulder on a motorway?
column2: In an emergency only.

column1: What is the minimum age for a Category B learner permit?
column2: 17.

column1: What must a learner driver display on the vehicle?
column2: L-plates on the front and rear.

column1: Must a learner driver be accompanied?
column2: Yes. By someone with a full, valid licence in the same category for at least 2 years.

column1: What is the seatbelt rule in a car?
column2: Everyone must wear a seatbelt where one is fitted; the driver is responsible for passengers under 17.

column1: What is the normal penalty point disqualification threshold for most fully licensed drivers?
column2: 12 points in a 3-year period.

column1: What is the lower penalty point disqualification threshold for learner and novice drivers?
column2: 7 points in a 3-year period.

column1: What is the purpose of the NCT?
column2: It is a basic roadworthiness and safety check for vehicles over 4 years old.

column1: Which lane should you normally use on a motorway?
column2: The left-hand lane unless overtaking or directed otherwise by signs or road markings.

column1: What must you do when a school warden shows the STOP sign?
column2: Stop and wait until children have crossed and the warden allows traffic to move again.

column1: What is the rule on mobile phones while driving?
column2: It is illegal to hold or use a hand-held mobile phone while driving; the safest option is not to use any phone while driving.

column1: What position should you take for a right turn in a one-way street?
column2: As close as practicable to the right-hand side.

column1: Where would you never make a U-turn?
column2: In a one-way street, where continuous white lines apply, or where a sign prohibits it.

column1: What should you look out for on country roads?
column2: Pedestrians, cyclists, animals, mud, concealed entrances, bends, and slow-moving farm machinery.

column1: When following the road ahead on a multi-lane dual carriageway, which lane should you normally use?
column2: Lane 1, the left-hand driving lane, unless signs or road markings say otherwise.

column1: What is the difference between a with-flow and a contra-flow bus lane?
column2: A with-flow lane runs with the traffic and can be used by buses, bicycles and taxis; a contra-flow lane runs against the traffic and is generally only for buses unless signs also allow cyclists.

column1: What is the difference between a pelican crossing and a zebra crossing?
column2: A pelican crossing is controlled by lights; a zebra crossing uses flashing amber beacons and pedestrian priority.

column1: What does an island in the middle of a pedestrian crossing mean?
column2: Treat each side of a zebra crossing as separate; a staggered pelican crossing is also treated as two crossings.

column1: Name 3 secondary controls you may be asked to demonstrate on the test.
column2: Examples: wipers, washers, demister, rear window heater, lights, or hazard lights.

column1: Name 3 technical checks you should be able to describe for the test.
column2: Examples: tyres, lights and indicators, oil, coolant, brake fluid, brakes, steering, or horn.

column1: What is the alcohol limit for learner, novice, and professional drivers?
column2: 20 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.
column3: official_core corrected safety_rules current_2026 web_image web_remote

column1: What is the alcohol limit for most other drivers?
column2: 50 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.

column1: What should you do before opening your car door?
column2: Check mirrors, look over your shoulder, and watch for cyclists or pedestrians.

column1: What should you do if you break down on a motorway?
column2: Pull onto the hard shoulder if possible, use your hazard lights, get help, and do not attempt roadside repairs unless it is necessary and safe.
